title: Nice'd test runs can wedge the whole -timeout in forkExec under host overload
body:
Observed once while verifying tick x73: `nice -n 15 go test -race -count=2 -timeout 45m -parallel 12 ./internal/exec/subprocess/` with host load ~17 (17 on 10 cores) timed out at 45m with TestAFreshDiskStartRefusesAPushedHeadThatIsNotThisAttemptSWork blocked 44m45s in syscall.forkExec — the forked child inherits the niced priority and was starved of every time slice while the rest of the suite completed around it. The identical command at normal priority (82.7s) and 10 isolated -race passes of the same test (4.9s) are green, so this is a machine-verdict episode of exactly the class cy2 fenced, not a tree defect: AGENTS.md tells workers to run heavy commands at low priority, and a worker doing so during an overload episode can lose 45 minutes to a wedge that re-runs green. Worth a tick to decide the repo's answer (a documented exception to the low-priority rule for fork-heavy suites, or a bounded per-suite retry), since -parallel 12 makes fork storms more frequent.
evidence: the command above; panic 'test timed out after 45m0s', running tests: TestAFreshDiskStartRefusesAPushedHeadThatIsNotThisAttemptSWork (44m45s), stack in syscall.forkExec/syscall.readlen; retried green 2026-10-08T01:57:29Z at load ~6
